core_motion_sentence: A dust-covered relic line is traced in white, then red sparks break the seal and the past rises as a Spirit, construct, or restored action.

timing.reduced_motion_fallback: static parchment reveal + icon swap; no dust swirl, no parallax, no pulsing spirits

motion_primitives.name: ArchiveTrace
motion_primitives.description: A thin ivory line traces a relic outline or card border like a conservator marking a find.

motion_primitives.name: RedSealBreak
motion_primitives.description: A red-orange crack crosses the trace, implying the dangerous thrill of discovery.

motion_primitives.name: DustLift
motion_primitives.description: Dust motes rise from a concealed layer, revealing title text or card metadata beneath.

motion_primitives.name: SpiritStatueRise
motion_primitives.description: A pale spirit silhouette lifts out of a statue or grave layer, then locks into a readable icon.

motion_primitives.name: RelicRebuild
motion_primitives.description: Broken bronze fragments snap into a doubled artifact outline.

motion_primitives.name: PrecedentStamp
motion_primitives.description: A soft white/gold seal stamps a decision point, implying order, precedent, and recorded truth.

placement_card.copy_tone: Use language of discovery, witness, relic, precedent, and revived action.

accessibility_rules: Dust and spirit particles must be decorative and hidden from assistive tech.
Do not use motion alone to communicate graveyard/relic/spirit state; include text or icon labels.
Honor prefers-reduced-motion by replacing particle movement with opacity and static state badges.
Maintain contrast between parchment backgrounds and bronze/red text; do not rely on pale gold for body copy.
implementation_notes: Lorehold should feel older, dustier, and more archaeological than Boros; avoid military-police visuals.
Red motion should read as discovery/adventure, not rage alone.
White motion should read as preservation/precedent, not bureaucracy alone.
The most distinctive Lorehold UI loop is: uncover -> classify -> revive -> act.
